blocks.text: Condo buildings in British Properties
Hawksley — 3963 Uplands Way (Uplands / Rodgers Creek)

A new condominium building by British Pacific Properties in collaboration with Beedie Living, in the Uplands community woven into the hillside of the British Properties. Current listings for units in the building state Freehold Strata title, Apartment/Condo sub-type, concrete construction, and year built 2025 in some listings and 2026 in others.
Where British Properties sits
Drive time to British Properties
And it is Uplands/Rodgers Creek product at the area's upper-west edge (listings classify the subdivision as Cypress Park Estates), not a building in the original subdivision.
Streets, schools and getting around British Properties

items.t: The British Properties is the wider master-planned hillside area developed by British Pacific Properties in the District of West Vancouver: the large-lot residential benches above Ambleside and Park Royal, from the Taylor Way side west across the Chartwell/Canterbury benches and up to the Rodgers Creek / Cypress Bowl Road lands.

Where the condo stock actually concentrates: only at the top of the area — the Rodgers Creek / Uplands lands on and around Uplands Way and Cypress Bowl Road, under site-specific Comprehensive Development (CD3) zoning, plus two small townhome pockets in Whitby Estates inside Chartwell. The original subdivision below is RS-zone detached houses; growth is directed by the OCP to the town and village centres, not into the Properties.

History anchor: the Properties were developed from the early 1930s by a group of British investors led by the Guinness family, which purchased most of the municipality's Upper Lands and built the Lions Gate Bridge (1937–38).

Main streets and transit: Taylor Way connects Marine Drive and Park Royal up into the Properties; Highway 1 (Upper Levels Highway) crosses above the original subdivision with access at Taylor Way and Cypress Bowl Road. TransLink route 254 (British Properties / Park Royal) climbs from Park Royal via Taylor Way, Southborough Drive, Eyremount Drive, Cross Creek Road, Chartwell Drive and Bonnymuir Drive, with selected trips to and from downtown Vancouver via the Lions Gate Bridge. Park Royal Exchange, at the area's foot, is the western terminus of the R2 RapidBus, which since September 7, 2026 runs one-seat through Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station.

Anchors inside the area: Chartwell Elementary (K–7), 1300 Chartwell Drive, and Sentinel Secondary (Grades 8–12), 1250 Chartwell Drive, sit beside each other on Chartwell Drive; Westcot Elementary (K–7), 760 Westcot Road, is at the foot of the Properties. The District's main indoor recreation facility serving the area is the West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre, 2121 Marine Drive in Ambleside, and the library is West Vancouver Memorial Library, 1950 Marine Drive.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in British Properties

items.t: British Properties covenants sit on top of zoning: Whether a specific strata lot in the Uplands or Whitby Estates carries a covenant step is a title-by-title check.

Hazard permits: an Environmental Development Permit is required for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank — the creeks crossing this hillside — and a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit is required for work within the Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area, described as within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface. Both are live checks for Uplands product at the forest edge.

blocks.text: Good to know about British Properties

items.t: The Properties' developer also built the bridge that made them possible. British investors led by the Guinness family purchased most of the Upper Lands and built the Lions Gate Bridge in 1937–38.

The "British Properties" name is not a District planning area. The OCP does not confirm an official planning-area name or boundaries for the Properties — its structure is the Ambleside Municipal Town Centre, Park Royal and the village centres — so strata, zoning and permit searches run on the street address and the CD3/RS zone, not on the neighbourhood name.
The growth cap above the benches is a fixed number: 974 homes.

Hawksley's amenity building is shared Uplands infrastructure. The project's feature list includes future access to The Studio, a three-storey amenity building for Uplands residents located adjacent to Hawksley, plus four electric bike shares — the amenity picture is community-scale, not building-only, and the "future access" wording means timing should be confirmed in the disclosure documents.

Two hazard permits ride on the forest-edge lots. Work within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface needs a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit, and work within 15 metres of a watercourse bank needs an Environmental Development Permit — the District has partnered with British Pacific Properties and the North Shore Mountain Bike Association on sanctioned trails in the Rodgers Creek–Marr Creek area between the second and fourth switchbacks of Cypress Bowl Road, on land owned by BPP and the District.

items.t: Where the townhouse stock concentrates: only in the two pockets named in the geography note — Whitby Estates on Garden Court / Highgrove Mews inside Chartwell, and the Hawksley podium on Uplands Way in the Rodgers Creek CD3 lands. The original subdivision below is RS-zone detached houses; the OCP directs growth to the town and village centres, not into the Properties.

Schools inside the area: Chartwell Elementary (K–7), 1300 Chartwell Drive, and Sentinel Secondary (Grades 8–12), 1250 Chartwell Drive, sit beside each other on Chartwell Drive; Westcot Elementary (K–7), 760 Westcot Road, is at the foot of the Properties.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in British Properties

items.t: District plans and zoning: District of West Vancouver Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 4985, 2018, and Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010 — never White Rock's Bylaw 2506/2220 pair, which belongs to White Rock only. Houses in the original subdivision sit in the RS single-family dwelling zones, while the Rodgers Creek lands sit in site-specific Comprehensive Development zones (CD3). The bylaw's ground-oriented dwelling rules state 4 dwellings maximum per lot, and 6 maximum if the site is wholly or partly within 400 metres of a prescribed bus stop.

West Vancouver taxes: District of West Vancouver 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid current taxes on July 2, 2026 and a further 5% on outstanding current taxes on September 2, 2026; water and sewer utilities are metered and billed quarterly. At British Properties values the Province's additional school tax commonly applies — 0.2% on the residential portion between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027.

The project's feature list includes future access to The Studio, a three-storey amenity building for Uplands residents located adjacent to Hawksley — the amenity picture is community-scale, not building-only, and the "future access" wording means timing should be confirmed in the disclosure documents.

Two hazard permits ride on the forest-edge lots. Work within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface needs a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit, and work within 15 metres of a watercourse bank needs an Environmental Development Permit — the District has partnered with British Pacific Properties and the North Shore Mountain Bike Association on sanctioned trails in the Rodgers Creek–Marr Creek area between the second and fourth switchbacks of Cypress Bowl Road, on land owned by BPP and the District.

blocks.text: Lots and land in British Properties
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Established-bench estate lots: detached houses on large hillside lots in the RS single-family dwelling zones of Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010 — the original subdivision is a single-family estate area, predominantly freehold detached; strata is concentrated in the Rodgers Creek / Uplands product above it and the small Whitby Estates pockets.

Lot character from the zone ladder, as stated: Section 200 minimum site areas are 8,094 m² in RS1, 1,625 m² in RS2, 975 m² in RS3, 731 m² in RS4 and 488 m² in RS5, with RS6 using the area of the site of record; the larger RS1/RS2 minimums are the ones associated with the Properties benches. These are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size; the zone for a specific lot is confirmed on the District's Zoning Map. Secondary suites and a detached secondary suite are among the permitted uses.
Covenant fabric — part of the land itself here: (Developer source.)

Serviced position, as the District states it: West Vancouver water and sewer utilities are metered and billed quarterly by the District — the serviced position for District lots as the District states it.
No ALR percentage split is stated; check any parcel on ALC mapping.

Hazard frame: creeks cross this hillside and the forest interface borders it — an Environmental Development Permit is required for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank, and a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit for work within the Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area (within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface).

blocks.text: Named developments above the subdivision

items.t: Mulgrave Park (Rodgers Creek area) — Estate Lots: British Pacific Properties' own site lists Estate Lots custom-home lots in Mulgrave Park, part of the Rodgers Creek area, among its British Properties communities. (Developer source.)
Hawksley (Uplands) — condo and townhome project by British Pacific Properties with Beedie Living: confirmed on the developer's own site. (Developer source.)

Rodgers Creek CD3 caps (District bylaw text): under the CD3 (Rodgers Creek) zone, Areas 5 and 6 are capped at 354 and 620 homes respectively (974 combined), with apartment buildings up to 16 storeys permitted; the District approved a 354-unit development permit for Area 5 (3900 Cypress Bowl Road) on July 8, 2025. These are zoning caps and a development permit.
Cypress Village Area: the District issued Development Permit 24-115 to British Pacific Properties Limited for initial works in the Cypress Village Area, above the original subdivision.

Sanctioned trails land note: the District has partnered with British Pacific Properties and the North Shore Mountain Bike Association on sanctioned trails in the Rodgers Creek–Marr Creek area of the Upper Lands, between the second and fourth switchbacks of Cypress Bowl Road, on land owned by BPP and the District — recreation land, not lot land.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around British Properties

items.t: Nearby areas: Ambleside and Park Royal (south, below Highway 1), Cedardale and Sentinel Hill (east, toward the Capilano River), Dundarave (west, below the benches), and Cypress Park / the Upper Lands (west and north-west).

Roads and transit: Taylor Way connects Marine Drive and Park Royal up into the Properties; Highway 1 (Upper Levels Highway) crosses above the original subdivision with access at Taylor Way and Cypress Bowl Road; the Lions Gate Bridge via Taylor Way and Marine Drive is the fixed crossing to Vancouver. TransLink route 254 (British Properties / Park Royal) climbs from Park Royal via Taylor Way, Southborough Drive, Eyremount Drive, Cross Creek Road, Chartwell Drive, Crestwell Road, Fairmile Road, King Georges Way, Robin Hood Road, Kenwood Road, Elveden Road, St. Andrews Road and Bonnymuir Drive to the Glenmore Drive terminus, with selected trips to downtown Vancouver. Park Royal Exchange is the western terminus of the R2 RapidBus, which since September 7, 2026 runs one-seat through Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station.

Civic anchors: West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre, 2121 Marine Drive in Ambleside; West Vancouver Memorial Library, 1950 Marine Drive; Park Royal at Marine Drive and Taylor Way is the OCP's regional shopping centre and Ambleside the Municipal Town Centre. Nearest hospital: Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in British Properties

items.t: Zoning — Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010: original-subdivision houses sit in the RS zones; the Rodgers Creek lands above sit in site-specific Comprehensive Development zones (CD3) instead. The bylaw's ground-oriented dwelling rules state 4 dwellings maximum per lot, and 6 maximum if the site is wholly or partly within 400 metres of a prescribed bus stop.

OCP — Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 4985, 2018: the District treats the British Properties as an established existing neighbourhood; growth is directed to the town and village centres (Ambleside, Park Royal, Dundarave, Caulfeild, Horseshoe Bay), not into the Properties.

SSMUH / added units as the District states it: Section 200 lists secondary suites and a detached secondary suite among permitted uses in the RS zones, and the ground-oriented rules above cap added dwellings per lot — eligibility and form are parcel-specific under Bylaw 4662; confirm with the District before pricing in suite potential.

Hazard Development Permits (District frame): Environmental Development Permit for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank; Wildfire Hazard Development Permit for work within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface. Check both on every hillside lot early.

Strata block (for the Uplands/Whitby strata a land buyer may pivot to): Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Properties ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.

blocks.text: Good to know about British Properties

items.t: The covenant step has no District equivalent (1930s origin): the Guinness-led venture that built the Lions Gate Bridge (1937–38) also left the registered building-scheme covenants — a buyer who budgets only for District permits has missed the BPP plan-approval application that gates every new build, extension, alteration, fence or structure.

The growth is all above the subdivision, by design: the OCP directs growth to Ambleside, Park Royal, Dundarave, Caulfeild and Horseshoe Bay — the Properties benches are an "established existing neighbourhood" in the plan — while 974 CD3 homes are capped in Rodgers Creek Areas 5–6 above. A bench lot's scarcity story and the Uplands supply story are both plan-documented.

Park Royal's tenure split is at the area's foot, not in it: part of Park Royal sits on Capilano IR No. 5 under the 1974 Park Royal Lease, split from District of West Vancouver ground — a leasehold diligence trap for any buyer who drifts east across Taylor Way assuming District fee-simple tenure.
